reader.requirement: At --std 85 a level-66 RENAMES entry (an elementary item when it renames one elementary item, a group when THRU is written or data-name-2 is a group) must stand outside the level hierarchy: it is neither subordinate to nor a superior of the entry before it, adds no storage to the record, is qualifiable only by its record, and leaves the level structure of the record it follows unchanged.
reader.edition-search: BindEntries' lvl == 66 arm never touches the level stack (no push, no pop) and attaches the alias to the open record's Renames66 list, not its Children; grep for CobolVersion/ConstructRegistry/IsAtLeast/DialectBehavior in DataBinder.cs around BindEntries/BindRenames and in DataBinder.RenamesEntry.cs finds none; LevelNumberPass's remarks state it is not edition-gated and it uses no edition API. The only edition touch is the diagnostic renderer choosing a §1985 citation.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb485_level_number_legal_forms exercises the level-number set and the 66 format; not the alias standing outside the hierarchy (record size, qualification, elementary-vs-group attributes)

probes.printed: L1 [17] [AB17] (ADD 5 TO an elementary RENAMES of PIC 99 B); L2 [7   ] (MOVE 7 TO a THRU RENAMES: a group/alphanumeric move); L3 [CD34] [WXYZ] (MOVE through R-GRP OF REC leaves REC2 alone); L4 04 04 04 02 (LENGTH of REC, G, R-GRP, R-NUM)
probes.expected: the record's size is unchanged by its 66 entries; an elementary RENAMES takes data-name-2's attributes (VI.5.11.4 GR2), a THRU RENAMES is a group (GR1); qualification by the 01 works

probes.printed: COBOL1639 on R-GRP OF G ('declared, but not under the given qualifier'); COBOL1639 on A OF R-GRP
probes.expected: the 66 entry is not subordinate to the intermediate group G and cannot itself be a qualifier (VI.5.11.3 SR3)

probes.printed: 66 entries after a record whose last entry is a level-10 item of a group bind and run ([CD12EFG] etc.); a following 01 REC2 opens a new record ([ZZYY])
probes.expected: no level relation between the 66 entries and the preceding entry

reader.notes: The level-66 arm of BindEntries handles a RENAMES entry before the level stack is consulted and binds it as an alias riding the record, so the entry has no level relation to its neighbours, as the rule says. Probes show the record size unchanged, qualification only through the 01, and elementary versus group behaviour per VI.5.11.4. Class a (variable length) does not apply beyond the SR6 bar on variable occurrence items, which is a separate rule.

refuter.evidence: lv3.cob: a 66 entry in the middle of a record, followed by a 05 entry, is refused COBOL2740 (§1985:VI.5.11.3 SR2), so a 66 never reopens or continues the level hierarchy. lv4.cob at --std 85: 66 entries after an FD record in the FILE SECTION (MOVE "WXYZ" TO a THRU-alias fills the record; FUNCTION LENGTH(SF-REC) is 04), after an 01 whose last item carries an 88 (the alias binds and B12 tests true), followed by a 77 and a new 01, and in the LINKAGE SECTION, all compile. The record length stays 04 with two 66 entries, and a MOVE 34 to the elementary alias R2 updates REC to [AB34]. That is: no level relation to the neighbouring entries, and no storage added. The reader's lvl2 qualification refusals stand. cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.3.2.1 GR1; OK §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR2.
